Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

must verb

have to: it has to be done

also have to, has to, had to, have got to, mustn’t, must not

classical

Sen. Ep. 119.3: ēsuriō: edendum est.
Ter. Ph. 318: tibi omne est exedendum

faciendum est

the gerundive with sum; the person who must, in the dative

it must be done; I must do it

The commonest way to say “must” and “have to”. Without an object it stands in the neuter (edendum est, I have to eat); with one, it agrees with it (tantum nivis fodiendum fuit, so much snow had to be dug).

Other words

  • necesse est — it is necessary, it has to be

    phrase, with an infinitive, an accusative and infinitive, or a bare subjunctive · also used · classical · Hor. S. 2.6.26: īre necesse est; Publil. Sent. N 32: Necesse est maximōrum minima esse initia.

    What cannot be otherwise: necessity, not duty (see necessary).

  • oportet, oportēre, oportuit — one must, it is right

    verb, impersonal · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 94.47: et discās oportet

    Of what is required or fitting (see should); with a bare subjunctive, discās oportet, you must learn.

  • nōn licet — you mustn’t (it is not allowed)

    phrase, with a dative of the person and an infinitive · also used · classical · Gell. 1.23.6: neque id dīcī licēre

    “Mustn’t” of a rule (see allow); said to someone as an order, nōlī with the infinitive (see don’t!). Nōn necesse est is “needn’t”.

Examples

  • ēsuriō: edendum est.

    I’m hungry: I must eat.Sen. Ep. 119.3

  • Tūte hoc intrīstī: tibi omne est exedendum.

    You cooked this up yourself: you have to eat it all.Ter. Ph. 318

  • nunc est bibendum, nunc pede līberō pulsanda tellūs

    now we must drink, now beat the ground with free feetHor. C. 1.37.1–2

  • tantum nivis fodiendum atque ēgerendum fuit

    so much snow had to be dug and carried awayLiv. 21.37.1

  • Necesse est maximōrum minima esse initia.

    The greatest things must have the smallest beginnings.Publil. Sent. N 32

  • et discās oportet et quod didicistī agendō cōnfirmēs

    you must both learn and make sure of what you have learnt by doing itSen. Ep. 94.47

  • puer respondit tacendum esse neque id dīcī licēre

    the boy answered that it had to be kept quiet and he was not allowed to tellGell. 1.23.6

See also should, necessary, allow, don’t!.
